newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge gets secret bugging files.
newsitem.headline: French judge gets secret bugging files.

text.p: French conservative ex-premier Alain Juppe, in a last-minute turnabout before his election defeat, gave a magistrate access to files on illegal wiretapping under late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand, police said on Thursday.

Police sources confirmed a report by the daily Le Monde that Juppe ordered the counter-intelligence agency DST last week to hand over "almost all" the files to investigating magistrate Jean-Michel Charpier.

Juppe had previously said the files were covered by state secrecy. They cover widespread illegal wiretapping of journalists, lawyers and politicians from 1982 to 1986 by Mitterrand's anti-terrorism unit.

Le Monde said some of the files were handed over to Charpier last Saturday, on the eve of a Socialist-led victory in parliamentary elections, and after the conservative Juppe said he would resign whatever the poll result.
The files were found in a garage rented by the former chief of the disbanded anti-terrorism unit, Christian Prouteau.
Several people are under investigation over the wiretapping, including Gilles Menage, who headed Mitterrand's private office.
Juppe reacted angrily when Menage recently decided to breach state secrecy and answer magistrates' questions in order to defend himself from suspicion that he authorised the bugging.
Juppe then said only he could decide whether to lift state secrecy. He said that any wiretapping that followed legal procedures was covered by official secrecy and the rest was not.
